correctness.rationale: Full cyclic-composition multiplicity \(n/k\) proved by rooted marked configurations; all-delegating atom counted separately. Ordered-pair shared-guru probabilities \(r^d+r^{n-d}-2r^n\) yield the exact squared-weight expectation. A logarithmic max-run union bound and finite-range square-reward variance \(O((\log n)^5/n)\) prove normalized Q convergence to \((2-q)/q\). Conditional weighted-sign triangular-array Lindeberg gives the Gaussian liquid-majority limit; independent random types give the direct binomial CLT and the strict frontier. Exact rational exhaustive verification covers all 24 \(n,q,p\) instances specified in VERIFICATION.md; infinite statements rely on proof, not enumeration. All assumptions, no-caster and tie boundaries are explicit.

value.rationale: The theorem solves a concrete motivated quantification: how much independent voting information is lost by local transitive delegation and when the increased caster expertise offsets that loss. The complete exact finite correct-tally distribution and a closed squared-weight identity are paired with a sharp nondegenerate local-alternative truth-tracking frontier, including distinct beneficial and harmful regimes (\(q=1/2\) threshold \(2/\sqrt3-1\)). The chosen \(n^{-1/2}\) regime is mathematically natural because fixed positive competence advantages can make both methods asymptotically perfect. This is more than a formal normalization, isolated negative check, or textbook special case; it provides interpretable exact parameters for an infinite family of local voting networks.
